review_note: Formats bounded operation, status and timing fields only when the download observer emits a diagnostic.
Captures the WinHTTP failure before teardown can change the thread error.
Disabled diagnostics skip the counter and clock. Enabled ones preserve the caller's thread error around the send-start log.
The scope emits one completion or failure record even on early returns and restores the thread error.
All three WinHTTP lifetimes use this destructor for the corresponding close on every exit.
Transfers the retained byte charge only if a queued job has not already reserved the capture. Holding the budget lock keeps both counters consistent.
Restores a temporary lease on every exit, including exceptions. Jobs that already own their reservation leave it intact.
Prefixes text and binary fields with their lengths so artwork can append directly to the key without building a second string.
Drops ownership of the checked capture and subtracts its outstanding charge, including on audit failure.
Measure the lock hold time and count the active, Ogg and ready entries visited on admitted events before replacing the full sum with deltas.
Accounts allocated capacity across each of the three stores, including unused capacity that still consumes the budget.
The size guard avoids scanning either collection in the common case. Over-limit entries get a recorded disposition before eviction.
Finds the oldest active capture only after the 32-entry cap is exceeded. An additional ordered index would also need updates on ordinary events.
Compares Ogg capture birth times under the same 32-entry overflow rule, independent of native decoder keys.
Records shutdown outcomes and checks completed captures before clearing all collections and their retained-byte charge.
Transparent lower_bound avoids temporary rejected keys. The entry cap and sequence comparison preserve newer records and tombstones.
Applies one encoded and decoded size limit for instance identifiers in both wire parsers.
Rejects spaces, control bytes and non-ASCII instance data in one bounded pass after decoding.
Validates that strtod consumed the field and produced a finite value. Each caller enforces its own range.
Uses one map lookup for optional and required flags and accepts precisely the wire values zero and one.
Computes block and remaining length directly from the offset, returning a borrowed view bounded by the initialized data.
Returns a pointer into the block for contiguous data. Only a crossing read fills reusable scratch storage.
Default construction starts with an invalid stage handle. Failed exclusive creation cannot claim another file.
Deleted copy construction prevents two objects disposing the same stage.
Deleted assignment prevents replacing a live stage handle or duplicating ownership.
Renames the held file and disarms its cleanup only after a successful commit.
Checks file size first and compares in 16 KiB chunks. Distinct error outcomes preserve retry decisions on incomplete reads.
Holds the compared object through disposal or transfer. A changed foreign file survives archive cleanup.
Reuses a verified destination or matching interrupted stage. Renaming by handle closes the pathname replacement race.
Emits a validated FLAC metadata block directly into the final buffer, with its three-byte length.
Rebuilds metadata blocks and appends the original audio once. Approved pictures avoid constructing a redundant cover block.
Clears partially produced output and supplies the specific parse or size failure to the caller.
Runs each mutation under the settings lock and signals the worker after releasing it. Failed changes do not advance the generation.
Changes the capture epoch, artifact revision and enrichment revision only for the settings that affect those consumers.
Routes both three-state controls through the same locked mutation and persistence signal.
Rejects menu changes to a hidden setting and writes the visible on/off value while holding the settings lock.
Updates the fast speed value without invalidating intact compressed audio. The caller validates the requested speed.
Swaps prepared paths under the lock and changes the destination revision only when root or folder mode changes.
Releases only the failed epoch and sequence. A late SQLite failure cannot erase a newer query or cache an absent date.
Guards the native play callback with the feature toggle and forwards to the current sorter, which owns the visible order.
Materializes playable UID/URI pairs once per sorted order. Rejects incomplete rows before creating a partial play context.
Passes the existing session items and player to the context updater. The optional callback permits older renderer builds.
Tests property writability before mutating the play command, including objects that cannot gain a missing property.
Reuses the sorted page and updates the clicked occurrence in Spotify's existing play request. Unrelated sessions and shuffle pass through.
Scans for a UID and checks its URI, preserving duplicate-track occurrences. Measure row-click latency before maintaining a second index.
Synchronizes only when a session has prepared playback items for the active sort mode.
Installs the shared context updater once and keeps the active order and successful update scoped to the renderer.
Clears the cached order, identity index and last update together so changing playlists releases their references.
Builds the UID index once per order. Session, provider, shuffle and sequence guards avoid rewriting unrelated or user-queued playback.
Applies a three-second retry delay after a failed update, leaving successful updates suppressed for the same session.
Returns the current player reference from the existing collector, avoiding another discovery pass on a playlist interaction.
Shares the encoding of known ID3 text frames and custom TXXX fields between full tagging and single-field insertion.
Inserts the frame before the existing ID3 bytes and preserves padding, unknown frames and audio. Measure allocations for large files before another rewrite.
Path callers construct one snapshot then reuse the same strict tri-state parser as startup.
Encodes the big-endian picture length separately from the little-endian Vorbis field lengths.
Borrows each field from the shared reader, handles picture comments separately and retains malformed-picture status for safe metadata updates.
Both renderer parsers share percent decoding and UTF-8 validation. Rejects incomplete escapes before advancing.
Centralizes rejection messages while leaving the caller's output record unchanged on parse failure.
Verifies the 40-character artwork identifier on an allowed CDN path before inserting it into the bounded references list.
Reads one file image and encoding for the startup consumers. A failed read remains distinguishable from a missing key.
Applies the same strict numeric choices and duplicate detection to fields read from the snapshot. The candidate list is small and startup-only.
Compares catalog fields that affect filename or identity before allowing an old path result to be reused.
Rejects changed generation, naming settings or root before the catalog comparison; equal inputs skip rebuilding paths.
Queues changed inputs immediately and coalesces probes for the same serial during the refresh interval.
Validates page size and lacing once per complete page and passes the layout to parsing. Partial input still returns the required byte count.
Checks prefix and the 22 alphanumeric identifier characters on borrowed text; shared by metadata and playback callers.
Supplies the track prefix at call sites which must exclude episode and album URIs.
Allows track and episode URIs through the same bounded character validator.
Keeps exclusive file ownership through the cap check and append; destructor closes the handle on formatter exceptions.
Defers request decoding and formatting until AppendDump verifies capacity under the write lock.
Defers building the summary string when the file is full; diagnostic counters are still available.
Searches the three short static toggle tables on a menu command. A separate index would duplicate the dispatch mapping.
Gives each submenu label the CEF string lifetime it needs during creation without repeating the conversion at each call.
Shares worker launch and failure cleanup for revealing the song folder or a recent file. Explorer work stays off the menu thread.
Decodes a four-byte little-endian field length without alignment assumptions. Bounds are checked by the caller.
Canonicalizes ASCII field names so case-insensitive replacements preserve unrelated comments.
Visits borrowed fields and rejects unreasonable counts or trailing data. FLAC and Ogg supply their framing separately.
Checks the remaining length before advancing and returns a view into the original comment rather than allocating each value.
Builds the replacement key set once per tagging operation and borrows fields retained for output.
Applies replacement and unkeyed-field policies while preserving borrowed values. Profile key normalization before changing the set representation.
Serializes retained fields, replacements and optional picture within the codec limit. Consider direct key/value append if tag construction measures hot.
Emits exactly four length bytes in wire order into the destination.
Checks remaining space for length plus payload before appending a field, so oversized metadata cannot wrap the limit.
Retries partial writes, advances only by confirmed bytes and limits each Win32 call to the representable DWORD count.
Captures the original play-action object so an identity assertion can verify that Saved sorting receives the native request intact.
Runs the real sorter in an isolated VM with a duplicate-URI playlist, an active session and a separate manual queue.
Supplies the mutable player state that individual tests change between sync attempts.
Records a deep copy of each context update so later test mutations cannot change the expected command history.
Checks idempotent sort updates, duplicate-row identity, unchanged playback position/manual queue, and reapplication to a new session.
Rejects unsuitable contexts, shuffle, unknown sessions and nonunique UID/URI matches before issuing a player command.
Defers while a queued item plays, releases silently, and only restores an explicitly supplied baseline.
Rejects players lacking the required methods or a readable state and verifies zero commands.
Injects a failing player state getter to exercise disconnected player handling.
Counts actual order-array reads and asserts repeated polling and a later context track do not traverse unchanged ordering again.
The Proxy counts numeric index reads while preserving the original element values through Reflect.get.
Verifies native shuffle suppresses sorted updates and the order is reapplied when shuffle ends.
A rejected async context command must leave only one attempt across subsequent renders.
Counts player updates and returns a rejected promise to exercise async failure handling.
Advances the event loop before polling again so the rejection has settled when call count is checked.
Asserts the same date generation incurs zero lookups and still detects host replacement of its items array.
Wraps the real Map getter with a counter to distinguish a true skipped lookup from a duplicate result.
Checks Saved order drives the next track, including duplicate occurrences, unsupported request contexts and reset.
Builds native playlist play requests with exact UID/URI/index and exposes the context entries the player would consume.
Default mutation leaves the synthetic native request unchanged in the ordinary play case.
Projects baseline entries to their native values for the host path when a request lacks explicit sorted pages.
Uses a different playlist URI to test that an unrelated play request remains untouched.
Requests shuffle to exercise the path that preserves native ordering.
Uses a search origin to verify Saved sorting does not rewrite play requests from another feature.
Supplies an absent UID to exercise refusal to select an unrelated duplicate occurrence.
Freezes options to verify unsupported nonwritable request shapes are left intact.
Verifies descending and ascending Saved orders update the active session and neutral mode restores every original row UID.
Supplies the synthetic current player to the same renderer lookup used in production.
Returns a known active playlist/session and context-track UID for playback synchronization.
Records the ordered context tracks and asserts the correct existing session receives the update.
Extracts UIDs from the updated page for comparison, preserving distinct occurrences with identical track URIs.
Derives the expected restored order from original row UIDs and compares the full list.
Sets a controllable monotonic clock to test fresh-date reuse and expiry at the 30-second boundary.
Substitutes a constant sort result so the heartbeat traversal counter measures only date selection and header painting.
Counts iteration of the stable URI set and delegates to its real iterator. The fresh-cache heartbeat must make zero traversals.
Preserves two different opaque FLAC PICTURE blocks in original order and confirms the upgraded audio stays intact.
Converts Windows TEMP to its WSL path and creates the requested fixture directory, centralizing shared runner setup.
Compiles the four MinHook translation units into the caller's object directory with distinct object names.
Compiles the minimp4, Vorbis and Ogg objects once per fixture suite, passing through compiler options to the audio build.
Seeds a shared artwork object into the metadata cache, so pinned-record tests exercise the same ownership path used for tagging.
Removes only the two temporary synthetic PE files and the per-run directory when architecture checks exit.
Satisfies the metadata pinning interface without enabling live metadata in the isolated directory-lookup fixture.
Waits until an exclusive SQLite transaction produces a retryable query failure or an unexpected reply, then asserts no reply was delivered.
Waits for the same request token to succeed after rollback, allowing the fixture to verify the retained saved date.
Tests release-audit memory ownership through queue transfer, queue-full fallback, allocation failure and concurrent capture, including exact-fit budgets.
Checks reused capture slots at wraparound copy header and payload while leaving unused destination bytes unchanged.
Compares published capture reservations to surviving capacities after pressure eviction, queue loss and shutdown, including audit failure.
Injects allocation failure or starts concurrent capture during validation and checks the temporary publication reservation remains visible.
Verifies validation released the budget lock and processes a real FLAC begin event while the audit retains its reservation.
Counts calls to the production path builder so unchanged heartbeats can be asserted to reuse computed paths.
Counts invocations while delegating to the actual payload decoder; verifies fast rejection can skip decoding.
Writes each generated header to a unique temporary file in its destination directory and atomically replaces the final header for concurrent runners.
Concatenates UTF-8 renderer assets in caller-specified order and delegates wide raw-string header generation to the atomic writer.
